title: Preservation, Cohen Forcing, and the Continuum

items.title: Closure, distributivity, and chain conditions for forcing orders
items.statement: Let kappa be an infinite regular cardinal and P a nonempty forcing preorder, with stronger conditions smaller. P is kappa-closed when every descending sequence of length gamma<kappa has a common lower bound; P is kappa-distributive when the intersection of every gamma<kappa dense open subsets of P is dense; and P is kappa-cc when every antichain has cardinality below kappa. Thus ccc is aleph_1-cc, while countably closed (sigma-closed) means aleph_1-closed, not omega-closed.
items.strategy: Fix the order orientation and strict length bounds. Relate the kappa-cc specialization to the published ccc definition, but do not identify closure with any chain condition.
items.axiom_base: ZF definition; later preservation theorems state their uses of AC

references.title: Karagila, Lecture Notes: Forcing & Symmetric Extensions, Definitions 3.20, 4.1 and 4.14, pp.18, 21, 23
Kunen, Set Theory, Chapter VII Definitions 6.7 and 6.12, pp.212–214

items.title: Closure, distributivity, and absence of new short sequences
items.statement: In ZFC, for an infinite regular kappa and a separative forcing order P, kappa-distributivity of P is equivalent to P adding no new sequences of ground-model elements of length below kappa. For an arbitrary forcing preorder the equivalence applies to its separative quotient. Every kappa-closed P is kappa-distributive. Hence kappa-closed forcing adds no new subsets of any ordinal gamma<kappa and preserves all ground-model cofinalities and cardinals at most kappa.
items.strategy: For closure, recursively strengthen a condition into each dense open set and take lower bounds at limits. Distributivity gives a common condition deciding every coordinate of a short name. Conversely, for separative P encode the generic's choices from a short sequence of maximal antichains as a ground-element sequence; if this sequence is decided, separativity makes one condition refine every antichain. For arbitrary preorders state the equivalence on the separative quotient. AC well-orders witness sets and selects deciding extensions. A new cofinal or collapse map below kappa would be a forbidden short sequence.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC chooses deciding extensions and ground-model enumerations

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Theorem 6.14 and Corollary 6.15, pp.214–215

items.title: Chain conditions preserve high cofinalities and ccc preserves cardinals
items.statement: In ZFC, if theta is regular and P is theta-cc, then forcing with P preserves every ground-model cofinality at least theta and every ground-model cardinal at least theta. In particular ccc forcing preserves all cofinalities and cardinals.
items.strategy: For a function name, choose for each argument a maximal antichain deciding its value. Theta-cc bounds every set of possible values below theta. Regularity prevents fewer than theta such small sets from being cofinal in a ground regular cardinal at least theta. Reduce arbitrary cofinality preservation to regular cardinals. Preserve cardinals directly: a forced surjection from mu<lambda onto a ground cardinal lambda>=theta has range inside the union of mu ground sets of size<theta, whose union has size<lambda, including the regular boundary lambda=theta. AC is used for maximal antichains, simultaneous choices, and cardinal union estimates; ordinal preservation is not silently upgraded.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used for maximal antichains and cardinal estimates

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Lemmas 5.5–5.10 and 6.8–6.9, pp.206–213

items.title: Nice names for subsets of a ground-model set
items.statement: For a forcing order P and ground-model set A, a nice P-name for a subset of A has the form union over a in A of {check(a)} times A_a, where every A_a is an antichain in P. No claim that an arbitrary name is nice is built into the definition.
items.strategy: Use the published check-name convention and set-coded forcing names. The next theorem supplies reduction to this form and the cardinal count.
items.axiom_base: ZF definition

items.title: Nice-name reduction and the ccc counting bound
items.statement: In ZFC, every P-name forced to be a subset of a ground-model set A is forced equal to a nice name. If P is ccc, |P|=mu is infinite, and |A|=lambda, then there are at most (mu^{aleph_0})^lambda nice names for subsets of A; in particular at most mu^{aleph_0} nice names for reals.
items.strategy: For each a choose by Zorn's lemma a maximal antichain among conditions forcing check(a) into the given name; the forcing theorem proves equality. Under ccc each antichain is countable. Encode a nice name by a lambda-sequence of countable subsets of P and apply cardinal exponentiation. AC is used exactly for the maximal antichains, simultaneous selection, and cardinal count.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used through Zorn's lemma and cardinal exponentiation

items.title: Cohen, collapse, and Lévy-collapse forcing orders
items.statement: For infinite kappa and nonzero lambda, Add(kappa,lambda)=Fn(lambda times kappa,2,<kappa), ordered by reverse inclusion. For infinite kappa<=lambda, Col(kappa,lambda)=Fn(kappa,lambda,<kappa). For an ordinal theta, the finite-condition Lévy order Lv(theta) consists of finite functions p on subsets of theta times omega with p(alpha,n)<alpha. Every definition is the ground-model set of such partial functions when used in forcing.
items.strategy: Verify that unions of compatible functions give common extensions and the empty function is largest. Keep Col(kappa,lambda), which adds a surjection kappa onto lambda, distinct from Lv(theta), which simultaneously collapses every nonzero alpha<theta to countable size.
items.axiom_base: ZF definition

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Definitions 6.1 and 8.6, pp.211, 231

items.title: Generalized delta systems for small supports
items.statement: In ZFC, let kappa be infinite and theta>kappa regular with |alpha|^{<kappa}<theta for every alpha<theta. Every theta-sized family of sets of cardinality below kappa has a theta-sized delta subsystem. In particular, if kappa is regular and rho=2^{<kappa}, a family of rho^+ many below-kappa subsets has a rho^+-sized delta subsystem.
items.strategy: Uniformize order types below kappa by regularity of theta. Code the union into theta, choose the least coordinate position whose values are unbounded, recursively thin to a theta-sequence separated above the bounded initial coordinates, and pigeonhole the common bounded part using |alpha|^{<kappa}<theta. For the rho=2^{<kappa} specialization require kappa regular to derive rho^{<kappa}=rho. AC supplies well-ordering, thinning, and cardinal estimates.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used for well-ordering and thinning

items.title: Closure and chain conditions of Cohen forcing
items.statement: In ZFC, if kappa is infinite regular and lambda>0, Add(kappa,lambda) is kappa-closed and has (2^{<kappa})^+-cc. Hence Add(omega,lambda) is ccc, and if 2^{<kappa}=kappa then Add(kappa,lambda) has kappa^+-cc.
items.strategy: A descending sequence of length below kappa has union of size below kappa. For the chain condition, apply the generalized delta-system lemma to domains and thin so root restrictions agree; two remaining functions have compatible union. At kappa=omega use the published finite delta-system theorem. AC supplies thinning and cardinal pigeonholes.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used in delta-system thinning

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Lemmas 6.10, 6.13 and Theorem 6.16, pp.213–215

items.title: Cardinal effects of collapse and Lévy-collapse forcing
items.statement: In ZFC, if kappa is regular and kappa<=lambda, Col(kappa,lambda) is kappa-closed and its generic union is a surjection kappa onto lambda. If theta is regular uncountable, Lv(theta) is theta-cc, collapses every nonzero alpha<theta to countable size, preserves theta, and therefore forces theta=aleph_1.
items.strategy: Meet coordinate and range dense sets to make generic unions total and onto. Closure of Col is by unions. For Lv(theta), apply the regular finite delta-system theorem to an alleged theta-antichain and thin so root values agree. Theta-cc keeps theta a cardinal while coordinate generics collapse all smaller ordinals. AC is used in delta-system and preservation steps.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used in chain-condition and preservation steps

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Lemmas 6.2, 8.7 and Theorem 8.8, pp.211, 231

items.title: Cohen coordinates are distinct and mutually generic
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a transitive ZFC model and $G$ be $M$-generic for $\operatorname{Add}(\omega,\lambda)$. For $\xi<\lambda$, $c_\xi(n)=(\bigcup G)(\xi,n)$ is a total real; distinct coordinates give distinct reals. For every partition $\lambda=I\mathbin{\dot\cup}J$ in $M$, the restrictions $G_I$ and $G_J$ are mutually generic and
$M[G]=M[G_I][G_J]=M[G_J][G_I]$.
items.strategy: Coordinate-domain dense sets give totality and a dense set deciding opposite fresh bits separates each pair. Identify Add with the product of its restrictions. For a dense set in one factor named over the other extension, form the ground-model dense set of pairs whose first component decides a member of the named dense set; meet it and repeat symmetrically. AC is only the ambient ZFC convention.
items.axiom_base: ZFC ground model

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VIII Theorem 1.4 and Chapter VII Lemma 5.3

items.title: Cohen forcing raises and, under a name count, fixes the continuum
items.statement: In ZFC, Add(omega,lambda) for infinite lambda preserves cardinals and forces 2^{aleph_0}>=lambda. If the ground model also satisfies lambda^{aleph_0}=lambda and lambda>=2^{aleph_0}, then it forces 2^{aleph_0}=lambda. In particular, over GCH, Add(omega,aleph_2) forces the continuum to be exactly aleph_2.
items.strategy: Coordinate reals inject lambda into the reals and ccc preserves lambda. Nice-name reduction bounds all extension reals by |P|^{aleph_0}=lambda^{aleph_0}. Combine inequalities; under GCH compute aleph_2^{aleph_0}=aleph_2. AC is used in preservation, names, and cardinal arithmetic.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; the exact aleph_2 clause assumes ground-model GCH

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Lemmas 5.13–5.14 and Corollary 5.15, pp.209–210

items.title: Higher Cohen forcing violates GCH at a regular cardinal
items.statement: In ZFC, let kappa be infinite regular and lambda>kappa satisfy 2^{<kappa}=kappa and lambda^kappa=lambda. Then Add(kappa,lambda) preserves all cardinals, adds lambda distinct subsets of kappa, and forces 2^kappa=lambda. Consequently, if lambda>=kappa^{++}, GCH fails at kappa. Over ground-model GCH, kappa=aleph_1 and lambda=aleph_3 give a cardinal-preserving extension with CH and 2^{aleph_1}=aleph_3.
items.strategy: Closure preserves cardinals at most kappa and kappa^+-cc preserves those at least kappa^+. Coordinate dense sets give lambda subsets. Generalize nice names to subsets of kappa; each coordinate carries an antichain below kappa^+, so at most lambda^kappa names occur. In the GCH instance closure adds no reals, preserving CH. AC supplies all cardinal computations and maximal antichains.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; the displayed instance assumes ground-model GCH

items.title: Easton-support orientation for many regular cardinals
items.statement: The single-regular-cardinal construction does not by naive iteration control an entire continuum function. Easton forcing uses support bounded below every regular cardinal to combine higher Cohen factors. Its permissible regular-cardinal patterns must be monotone and satisfy cf(F(kappa))>kappa. This page records only that orientation, not Easton's theorem or singular-cardinal control.
items.strategy: Explain why full or naive finite support can destroy closure or collapse cardinals, state the bounded-support idea and the monotonicity/König restrictions, and stop before claiming the global realization theorem.
items.axiom_base: ZFC orientation only

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII after Theorem 6.18 and Chapter VIII §4, pp.216–217, 259–270
Karagila, Theorem 5.20 and Easton-support remark, pp.28–29

items.title: Fixed finite-fragment verification for the Cohen countermodels
items.statement: For each externally fixed finite fragment $\Delta$ of $\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{CH}$, and likewise of $\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{GCH}$, the Cohen forcing argument admits a finite ZFC verification for $\Delta$ of the kind required by [[lem-forcing-transfer-for-finite-zfc-fragments]]. Consequently ZFC proves that a model of that particular $\Delta$ exists. This is an externally indexed assertion about each fixed fragment; it does not assert a PA-verified uniform proof-code constructor.
items.strategy: For each fixed finite target fragment, select the actual forcing axioms and schema instances, apply Add(omega,(2^aleph_0)^+), use ccc/cardinal preservation and distinct coordinate reals, then invoke finite forcing transfer. No PA constructor is certified.
items.axiom_base: Externally indexed ZFC fixed-fragment proofs

items.title: Externally fixed-fragment relative consistency of not CH and not GCH
items.statement: Externally, $\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC})$ implies each of $\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{CH})$ and $\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{GCH})$. The implication here is a metatheorem obtained by applying a separate finite-fragment construction to any purported contradiction proof; no PA proof of a uniform refutation transformer is claimed.
items.strategy: If $\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{CH}$ were inconsistent, a contradiction proof would use only a finite set $\Delta$ of its axioms. Fix that $\Delta$ externally. F1 gives a ZFC proof of the existence of a model of $\Delta$. Soundness for the finite proof shows that no such model exists, so ZFC itself would be inconsistent. Contraposition gives the first consistency implication. The same argument with a finite refutation of $\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\mathrm{GCH}$ and the second F1 construction gives the other implication. Both are external consequences of fixed-fragment proofs; the positive consistency counterparts are separate results.
items.axiom_base: PA

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VII Corollary 5.15 and §9, pp.209–210, 232–234

title: Preservation, Cohen Forcing, and the Continuum: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A nice name for one Cohen coordinate
items.statement: For xi<lambda, the canonical Add(omega,lambda)-name whose n-th antichain consists of conditions assigning value 1 at (xi,n) is a nice name and evaluates to the set of 1-bits of c_xi.
items.strategy: Check the antichain coordinatewise and evaluate the name directly against G, comparing it with the generic union.
items.axiom_base: ZF verification inside the ZFC forcing context

items.title: The Lévy collapse of a regular uncountable cardinal
items.statement: For regular uncountable theta, Lv(theta) makes every alpha<theta countable while preserving theta, so theta is exactly the new aleph_1; the example displays the dense sets making each coordinate map omega onto alpha.
items.strategy: Use domain and range dense sets for each coordinate, then invoke theta-cc preservation, keeping collapse below theta separate from preservation at theta.
items.axiom_base: ZFC

references.title: Kunen, Definition 8.6, Lemma 8.7 and Theorem 8.8, p.231

items.title: Two Cohen reals as mutually generic coordinates
items.statement:
Let $M$ be a transitive ZFC model and let $G$ be $M$-generic for $\operatorname{Add}(\omega,2)$. Write $c_i(n)=(\bigcup G)(i,n)$ for $i<2$. The forcing $\operatorname{Add}(\omega,2)$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Add}(\omega,1)\times\operatorname{Add}(\omega,1)$. Its coordinate reals satisfy
$M[c_0,c_1]=M[c_0][c_1]=M[c_1][c_0]$, and each is Cohen-generic over the extension by the other.
items.strategy: Write the restriction/union isomorphism, translate rectangular dense sets, apply mutual genericity, and exhibit the dense set forcing a disagreement.
items.axiom_base: ZFC ground model

items.title: Every ccc forcing is countably closed
items.statement: False claim: every ccc forcing is countably closed (sigma-closed).
items.strategy: Add(omega,1) is countable and ccc. The descending sequence fixing successively more bits has no finite-function lower bound, so it is not sigma-closed; it also adds a new real, while sigma-closed forcing adds no new omega-sequence. Omega-closed under the strict <omega convention is not the intended claim.
items.axiom_base: ZFC

items.title: Two-step forcing iterations
items.statement: For set-sized P with a largest condition and a P-name dot Q forced to be a nonempty forcing preorder with a largest condition, close the names occurring in dot Q under immediate subnames to form a set U, and let R be the names contained in U x P. The set-sized P*dot Q consists of pairs (p,dot q) with dot q in R and p forcing dot q in dot Q, ordered by p<=p' and p forcing dot q<=dot q'. Under AC every unrestricted local pair has a forced-equal representative in this carrier.
items.strategy: Use Power Set for the set-sized name carrier; under AC mix the names occurring in dot Q over a maximal antichain below p to prove local forced-equivalence density. Verify the order modulo forced equality and defer generic factorization and ccc preservation to the next theorem.
items.axiom_base: ZF definition

items.title: Generic factorization and ccc preservation for two-step iterations
items.statement: In ZFC, a P*dot Q-generic K factors as a P-generic G and dot Q_G-generic H with M[K]=M[G][H], and conversely G*H is generic. If P is ccc and P forces dot Q ccc, then P*dot Q is ccc.
items.strategy: Project K to G, evaluate second coordinates to H, and translate dense sets both ways using forced-equal representatives in the set-sized carrier. For ccc, index an alleged omega_1-antichain by ground ordinals, form the P-name I of indices whose first coordinates enter the generic, and prove syntactically that I injects into a forced Q-antichain. Forced ccc of Q makes I countable; preservation of omega_1 by P and a countable predense antichain give one ground bound on I, contradicting the indexed antichain. AC supplies maximal antichains and enumerations.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used for maximal antichains and enumerations

items.title: Finite-support forcing iterations
items.statement: An ordinal-length finite-support iteration is recursively defined from set-indexed (P_alpha,dot Q_alpha,dot 1_alpha) data, with each distinguished dot 1_alpha in the bounded carrier R_alpha forced to be a largest iterand condition. P_0 is trivial, P_{alpha+1}=P_alpha*dot Q_alpha, and at a limit delta a condition is a coherent function on delta taking its alpha-coordinate in R_alpha with finite support relative to dot 1_alpha, ordered coordinatewise by earlier forcing relations. Supplied top names fill coordinates outside support; this definition needs no Choice.
items.strategy: Use the bounded set carriers R_alpha from the two-step definition and supply distinguished top names as part of the iterand data. State the recursion with each limit coordinate in R_alpha, restrict conditions to earlier stages, make support finiteness part of membership, and use Replacement to form the all-top function without Choice.
items.axiom_base: ZF definition

items.title: Restriction maps and complete embeddings in an iteration
items.statement: For alpha<=beta, restriction sends p to p|alpha, and top-padding embeds P_alpha completely into P_beta. Incompatibility of two P_alpha-conditions is preserved and reflected by this embedding; no such claim is made for arbitrary restrictions of P_beta-conditions. A P_beta-generic restricts to P_alpha-generic, the stages form an increasing chain, and successor quotients are the evaluated iterands.
items.strategy: Induct on beta. Show that p|alpha is a reduction of p: every extension of p|alpha in P_alpha is compatible with p after a suitable amalgamation. This proves completeness and the generic restriction claim; apply two-step factorization at successors and compose at limits.
items.axiom_base: ZF order theory

items.title: Finite-support iterations of ccc forcing are ccc
items.statement: In ZFC, if every $P_\alpha$ forces $\dot Q_\alpha$ ccc, then every $P_\beta$ of the finite-support iteration is ccc.
items.strategy: Induct on beta. Successors use two-step ccc. At a limit, delta-system the supports of an alleged uncountable antichain, put the finite root below an earlier stage, find compatible restrictions there, and amalgamate disjoint petals. AC enters through delta-system thinning.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used in delta-system thinning

items.title: Small sets of ground ordinals are captured at a bounded iteration stage
items.statement: In ZFC, let $\delta$ have uncountable cofinality and $P_\delta$ be a finite-support ccc iteration. In a $P_\delta$-extension, every set $A$ of ground-model ordinals with $|A|<\operatorname{cf}(\delta)$ belongs to some $V[G_\alpha]$, $\alpha<\delta$. The same holds for structures and indexed families coded by such sets.
items.strategy: Choose a ground-indexed name for a surjection onto the small set and countable maximal antichains deciding each ordinal value. Bound their finite supports, normalize to literal top-padded conditions, and construct a new labelled intermediate-stage name from the restricted antichains. AC selects antichains and codes; ccc preserves cf(delta).
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used for names, coding, and support selection

items.title: Size bound for finite-support ccc iterations
items.statement: In ZFC, let $\mu$ be infinite with $\mu^{\aleph_0}=\mu$. If a finite-support iteration has length at most $\mu$ and every iterand is forced ccc and to have cardinality below $\mu$, then it can be replaced stage by stage by a forcing-equivalent coherently coded presentation in which every $P_\alpha$ has cardinality at most $\mu$. Equivalently, each original stage has a dense suborder of cardinality at most $\mu$; no bound is asserted for redundant names in an arbitrary raw presentation.
items.strategy: Induct on alpha while choosing dense coded presentations. At a successor, force an enumeration of the iterand by an ordinal below mu and use countable deciding antichains to choose at most mu^{aleph_0}=mu canonical representatives; at a limit use finite tuples from prior coded stages. Prove the chosen representatives dense and the replacement forcing-equivalent. AC supplies the enumerations, coherent choices, and arithmetic.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used for enumerations and name counts

items.title: Martin's Axiom at a cardinal and Martin's Axiom
items.statement:
Work in ZFC. For an infinite cardinal $\kappa$, $\mathrm{MA}(\kappa)$ says that whenever $P$ is a nonempty ccc forcing **partial order** and $\mathcal D$ is a family of at most $\kappa$ dense subsets of $P$, there is a filter $G\subseteq P$ meeting every member of $\mathcal D$. Here filters use the stronger-is-smaller convention. Replacing each $D$ by its downward closure shows that dense and dense-open formulations agree.

**Martin's Axiom**, MA, is the scheme $\mathrm{MA}(\kappa)$ for every infinite $\kappa<2^{\aleph_0}$. The inequality is strict; $\mathrm{MA}(2^{\aleph_0})$ is not included.
items.strategy: Reuse the stronger-is-smaller filter convention and make the strict continuum bound explicit, so MA(2^{aleph_0}) is not asserted.
items.axiom_base: ZFC statement scheme

references.title: Karagila, Definition 7.1 and MA convention, p.35

items.title: MA(aleph_0) and the implication from CH to MA
items.statement: In ZFC, MA(aleph_0) holds for every nonempty preorder, without ccc. Consequently CH implies MA, because under CH every infinite cardinal below the continuum is aleph_0.
items.strategy: Enumerate the dense family and recursively choose a descending condition in the next dense set; its upward closure is the filter. AC supplies enumeration and choices. Under CH no larger infinite kappa remains in MA's quantifier.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; countable dependent choices follow from AC

items.title: Martin's Axiom reduces to small ccc orders
items.statement: In ZFC, for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, $\mathrm{MA}(\kappa)$ is equivalent to its restriction to ccc forcing orders of cardinality at most $\kappa$. A largest condition may be adjoined, and any such small order can be coded on a subset of a fixed set of cardinality $\kappa$.
items.strategy: Choose countable maximal antichains refining the dense sets and close their union under compatibility and dense-extension witnesses. The suborder has size at most kappa, reflects compatibility, and retains dense sets. A filter there generates one in the original. AC supplies antichains and hull choices.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; AC is used for maximal antichains and the hull

references.title: Kunen, Chapter II Lemma 3.1 and Chapter VIII Lemma 6.2, pp.62–63, 278–279

items.title: The omega_2 bookkeeping iteration for MA
items.statement:
Assume ground-model GCH. At each stage choose, as part of the recursion, a coherent dense coded suborder $D_\alpha\subseteq P_\alpha$ of size at most $\aleph_2$ using [[lem-finite-support-iteration-size-bound]]. Fix a well-order of $H(\aleph_3)$ and a bookkeeping map on $\omega_2$ that repeats every relevant **canonical nice code over an earlier $D_\alpha$** cofinally often. The **$\omega_2$ MA iteration** is the finite-support iteration $\langle P_\alpha,\dot Q_\alpha,\dot1_\alpha:\alpha<\omega_2\rangle$ in which bookkeeping selects a coded candidate name for an order on a subset of $\aleph_1$. Choose a maximal antichain deciding whether that candidate is a ccc order of the required size. On each positive branch, use its top-adjoined version as in [[lem-ma-reduction-to-small-ccc-orders]]; on each negative branch, use the one-point order. Mix those branch names into the single name $\dot Q_\alpha$, including a branchwise name $\dot t_\alpha$ for its largest condition. Thus $P_\alpha$ forces that the iterand is nonempty, ccc, and has $\dot t_\alpha$ as a largest condition. A candidate already forced ccc is used, with its adjoined top, on every branch. Cohen forcing, with a top adjoined, is selected at cofinally many stages.

The local mixed top name $\dot t_\alpha$ need not lie in the prescribed set-sized carrier $R_\alpha$. Apply the AC/maximal-antichain mixing clause of [[def-two-step-forcing-iteration]] at $1_{P_\alpha}$ to choose $\dot1_\alpha\in R_\alpha$ forced equal to $\dot t_\alpha$. Recursively choose these representatives as part of the set-indexed stage data, so the all-top condition and literal top padding required by [[def-finite-support-forcing-iteration]] are defined at every stage.

The bookkeeping enumerates canonical codes, not arbitrary raw $P_\alpha$-names. Given a name which a condition forces to be a ccc order of size at most $\aleph_1$, first use ambient AC to name an isomorphic presentation on a subset of $\aleph_1$. Encode its domain and order relation as a subset of the fixed ground set $\aleph_1\times\aleph_1$. Below a coded $D_\alpha$-condition, apply [[thm-nice-name-reduction-and-counting]] using countable deciding antichains from the dense ccc suborder $D_\alpha$; this gives an equivalent nice code over $D_\alpha$. By GCH there are at most $(\aleph_2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_1}=\aleph_2$ such codes at each stage. The coherent coding and schedule revisit each earlier canonical code later, while the raw presentation may have unboundedly many forced-equal names. AC chooses the master well-order, deciding antichains, carrier representatives, and scheduling map. The branch mixture makes “$\dot Q_\alpha$ is ccc” forced by $P_\alpha$ rather than merely decided by some conditions; it never discards a positive branch merely because the top condition did not decide it.
items.strategy: Use the size lemma to code stages/names in aleph_2. AC chooses a master well-order and f:aleph_2 onto aleph_2 times aleph_2 with earlier codes repeated later. A maximal-antichain mixture makes each iterand forced ccc. The next theorem proves exhaustiveness and the forcing effect.
items.axiom_base: ZFC plus ground-model GCH; AC chooses well-ordering/bookkeeping

items.title: The omega_2 iteration forces MA and continuum aleph_2
items.statement: Over a ZFC+GCH ground model, the omega_2 bookkeeping iteration is ccc and forces MA together with 2^{aleph_0}=aleph_2, hence not CH.
items.strategy: Finite-support ccc preserves cardinals. Name counting bounds reals by aleph_2; cofinally inserted Cohen stages give aleph_2 distinct reals. For a final small ccc Q and dense family, reduce/codify and capture them at a bounded stage; ccc absoluteness follows because earlier antichains remain uncountable in the final ccc extension. Bookkeeping forces with Q later and its coordinate generic meets all earlier dense sets. AC supplies codes and well-orders.
items.axiom_base: ZFC plus ground-model GCH; AC used in bookkeeping/name counts

items.title: Fixed finite-fragment verification for the MA iteration
items.statement: For every externally fixed finite fragment $\Delta$ of $\mathrm{ZFC}+\mathrm{MA}+\neg\mathrm{CH}$, there is a finite fragment $\Gamma$ of ZFC such that ZFC proves the existence of a model of $\Delta$ by the constructible-ground and finite-support $\omega_2$-iteration argument. The fragment and its proof may depend on $\Delta$; no PA-verified uniform refutation transformer is asserted.
items.strategy: For each fixed finite target fragment, collect the MA instances and finite iteration proof support, obtain the needed GCH source through L, reflect a finite source model and force with the omega_2 iteration.
items.axiom_base: Externally indexed ZFC fixed-fragment proofs; AC in object iteration

references.title: Kunen, Chapter VIII Theorem 6.3 and Corollary 6.4, pp.279–281; Chapter VII §9, pp.232–234

items.title: Externally fixed-fragment relative consistency of MA and not CH
items.statement: Externally, $\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC})$ implies $\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{ZFC}+\mathrm{MA}+\neg\mathrm{CH})$. This is a fixed finite-fragment metatheorem, without a claim that PA verifies a uniform proof-code reduction.
items.strategy: A contradiction proof in $\mathrm{ZFC}+\mathrm{MA}+\neg\mathrm{CH}$ uses some finite set $\Delta$ of target axioms, including finitely many MA instances. Apply F1 to that particular $\Delta$. ZFC proves that a model of $\Delta$ exists, while the alleged contradiction proof and finite-model soundness give a ZFC proof that no such model exists. Thus a target inconsistency would imply a ZFC inconsistency. Contraposition yields the displayed external relative-consistency implication. No assertion about PA verification of the fragment-selection map is needed.
items.axiom_base: PA

items.title: A continuum-sized almost-disjoint family on omega
items.statement: In ZFC there is an almost-disjoint family of infinite subsets of omega of cardinality 2^{aleph_0}.
items.strategy: Enumerate finite binary sequences by omega and send each infinite branch to the codes of its finite initial segments. Distinct branches share only finitely many nodes; injectivity gives continuum size. No arbitrary selection is needed after fixing the coding.
items.axiom_base: ZFC; construction itself is choice-free

items.title: Cardinal exponentiation below the continuum under MA
items.statement: In ZFC+MA, for every infinite kappa<2^{aleph_0}, 2^kappa=2^{aleph_0}. Consequently the continuum is regular.
items.strategy: Use kappa members of the almost-disjoint family. For each X subseteq kappa, a common-finite-stem ccc order yields by MA a real meeting A_alpha infinitely exactly for alpha in X. Thus P(kappa) injects into the reals; monotonicity gives the reverse inequality. König then gives regularity. AC supplies cardinal indexing.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+MA; AC used for cardinal indexing

items.title: MA makes unions of fewer than continuum many meagre sets meagre
items.statement: In ZFC+MA, the union of fewer than $2^{\aleph_0}$ meagre subsets of the real line is meagre. In particular every set of reals of cardinality below the continuum is meagre.
items.strategy: Use AC to replace each meagre set by a sequence of closed nowhere dense sets and flatten. Enumerate rational intervals and use the standard ccc almost-disjoint finite-condition order to select countably many dense open unions whose complements cover the original union. Singleton sets give the final clause. Do not use the published sigma-ideal proposition, whose deps omit its stated countable-choice hypothesis.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+MA; AC selects nowhere-dense witnesses/enumerations

items.title: MA makes unions of fewer than continuum many null sets null
items.statement: In ZFC+MA, the union of fewer than $2^{\aleph_0}$ Lebesgue-null subsets of the real line is null. In particular every set of reals of cardinality below the continuum is null.
items.strategy: For epsilon>0 order open sets of measure below epsilon by enlargement; covering each null set is dense by outer regularity. Prove ccc by symmetric-difference approximation with finite unions of rational intervals and uncountable thinning. An MA filter's union has measure at most epsilon because finite unions remain conditions and the rational base yields a countable cofinal subfamily. Repeat for epsilon tending to zero and use completeness. AC supplies thinning and choices.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+MA; AC used in ccc thinning and family selections

items.title: Under MA(aleph_1), arbitrary products of ccc spaces are ccc
items.statement: In ZFC, $\mathrm{MA}(\aleph_1)$ implies the product of two ccc spaces is ccc and consequently every product of ccc spaces is ccc.
items.strategy: Use MA(aleph_1) to thin an omega_1-family of opens in one factor to an uncountable finite-intersection family; rectangle projections then prove binary products. Induct for finite products. Delta-system the finite supports of basic opens in an alleged uncountable disjoint family in an arbitrary product and project incompatibility to the finite root. AC chooses rectangles and thins.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+MA(aleph_1); AC used for basic-open choices and thinning

references.title: Kunen, Theorem 1.9, Lemma 2.23 and Theorem 2.24, pp.50–51, 61

title: Finite-Support Iterations and Martin's Axiom: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A two-step Cohen iteration is a product
items.statement: When dot Q is the constant check-name for Add(omega,1), Add(omega,1)*dot Q is forcing-equivalent to Add(omega,2), and its extension adjoins two mutually generic Cohen reals in either order.
items.strategy: Identify the dense check-name suborder of the set-sized two-step iteration with the two-coordinate finite-function order, then apply factorization.
items.axiom_base: ZFC ground model

items.title: MA produces a real outside a small listed family
items.statement: Assume MA(kappa). Given at most kappa reals, the Cohen finite-function order and coordinate-domain/disagreement dense sets produce a real distinct from every listed real. Hence MA(kappa) implies kappa<2^{aleph_0}.
items.strategy: Require every coordinate to be defined and a disagreement with every listed real. The countable Cohen order is ccc; the MA filter's union is total and new.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+MA(kappa)

items.title: A small set of reals is both null and meagre under MA
items.statement: Under MA, if X is a set of reals with |X|<2^{aleph_0}, then X is both Lebesgue null and meagre, though these notions are independent for arbitrary sets.
items.strategy: Write X as the union of its singleton subsets. Each singleton is closed nowhere dense and null. Apply the two union theorems separately.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+MA

items.title: Martin's Axiom implies CH
items.statement: Martin's Axiom implies the Continuum Hypothesis.
items.strategy: Assuming ZFC is consistent, F2 gives the consistency of a theory in which MA holds and CH fails. Thus the implication is not a theorem of ZFC, on the same metatheoretic consistency assumption under which the false statement is posed. F1 records that reversing the arrows would confuse the valid implication with its false converse. The refutation rests on the fixed-fragment model argument of F2; it does not assume a countable transitive model of full ZFC.
items.axiom_base: PA formalizes the relative-consistency refutation over ZFC

references.title: Kunen, Lemma 2.6 and Chapter VIII Theorem 6.3, pp.54–55, 279–281
